questions.question: Which of the following is responsible for the dispersion of white light through a glass prism?

options.text: Different colours of light travel at different speeds in glass.
White light contains only one colour.
Different colours of light travel at the same speed in glass.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Different colours of light travel at different speeds in glass.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Dispersion of white light** occurs when white light passes through a glass prism. It splits into its constituent colors, forming a spectrum (VIBGYOR: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red).
 
• This phenomenon is due to the fact that **different colors of light travel at different speeds in glass**. Each color has a different wavelength, and the refractive index of glass varies with the wavelength of light.
 
• **Violet light** bends the most, while **red light** bends the least. This is because violet has the shortest wavelength, and red has the longest wavelength among the visible spectrum.
 
• The separation of white light into its constituent colors is referred to as **dispersion**.

questions.question: When the velocity of a body is increased to twice its original value, its kinetic energy becomes _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**four times the original value**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy (KE)** is given by the formula: *KE = (1/2)mv²*, where **m** is the mass of the body and **v** is its velocity.
 
• When the velocity **v** is doubled, the new velocity becomes **2v**.
 
• Substituting the new velocity into the formula, the new kinetic energy becomes: *KE' = (1/2)m(2v)² = (1/2)m(4v²) = 4 × (1/2)mv²*.
 
• This shows that the kinetic energy increases by a factor of **4** when the velocity is doubled.
 
• *Hence, the kinetic energy becomes four times the original value__ when the velocity is doubled.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Kinetic Energy:**

 
 
• **Kinetic Energy** is a type of mechanical energy associated with a body in motion. It depends on the **mass** and **velocity** of the body.
 
• It is a scalar quantity and is always positive.
 
• The SI unit of Kinetic Energy is the **joule (J)**.
 
• **Example:** A moving car, a flying airplane, and a rolling ball all have kinetic energy.
 
 
 
• **Effect of Velocity on Kinetic Energy:**
 
 
• Kinetic Energy is directly proportional to the square of the velocity of the body. This means that a small change in velocity has a significant impact on kinetic energy.
 
• For instance, if velocity is tripled, the kinetic energy increases by a factor of **9** (3²).
 
• Similarly, reducing the velocity to half will decrease the kinetic energy to **one-fourth** of its original value.
 
 
 
• **Relation with Mass:**
 
 
• Kinetic Energy is directly proportional to the **mass** of the body. If the mass is doubled, the kinetic energy also doubles, assuming velocity remains constant.
 
• This implies that heavier objects moving at the same speed have more kinetic energy than lighter ones.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• **Transport:** Kinetic Energy is critical in understanding vehicle motion, fuel efficiency, and safety measures like braking systems.
 
• **Energy Generation:** Hydropower plants use the kinetic energy of flowing water to generate electricity.
 
• **Sports:** In games like cricket or football, the kinetic energy of the ball determines its speed and impact.
 
 
 
• **Important Facts:**
 
 
• The **Work-Energy Theorem** states that the work done on an object is equal to the change in its kinetic energy.
 
• Kinetic Energy is a component of **mechanical energy**, which also includes potential energy.
 
• In a closed system with no external forces, the total mechanical energy (kinetic + potential) remains conserved.

questions.question: A solution is said to be stable when:

options.text: the solute particles float on the surface of solution when left undisturbed
the solute particles settle down when left undisturbed
the solute particle forms a separate layer with solvent particles
the solute particles do not settle down when left undisturbed

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the solute particles do not settle down when left undisturbed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A solution is considered **stable** when the solute particles are uniformly distributed throughout the solvent and do not settle at the bottom when left undisturbed. This ensures the solution remains homogeneous over time.
 
• In a stable solution, the **solute particles** are dissolved at the molecular or ionic level in the solvent, forming a single-phase system (e.g., salt dissolved in water).
 
• Option 1 is incorrect as solute particles floating on the surface indicate incomplete dissolution, leading to an unstable solution.
 
• Option 2 is incorrect because solute particles settling down when left undisturbed indicates it is a suspension, not a solution.
 
• Option 3 is incorrect as the formation of a separate layer signifies immiscibility, often seen in mixtures like oil and water.
 
• **Stable solutions** are typical of true solutions such as sugar in water or alcohol in water. These solutions are characterized by transparency and uniform composition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Solutions:**

 
 
• **True Solution:** Homogeneous mixture where solute particles are less than 1 nm in size (e.g., sugar in water).
 
• **Colloidal Solution:** Heterogeneous mixture where solute particles range between 1-100 nm and do not settle down (e.g., milk).
 
• **Suspension:** Heterogeneous mixture where solute particles are larger than 100 nm and settle down over time (e.g., sand in water).
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Stability of a Solution:**
 
 
• **Temperature:** Increasing temperature often increases solubility, enhancing stability.
 
• **Nature of Solvent and Solute:** Polar solvents dissolve polar solutes, while nonpolar solvents dissolve nonpolar solutes.
 
• **Concentration:** Over-saturation can lead to precipitation, reducing stability.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Stable Solutions:**
 
 
• Salt dissolved in water.
 
• Alcohol mixed with water.
 
• Vinegar (acetic acid in water).
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• **Pharmaceutical Industry:** Preparation of syrups and injectables.
 
• **Food Industry:** Beverages and flavoring solutions.
 
• **Chemical Industry:** Solutions for reactions and processes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **True Solution Characteristics:**

 
 
• Particle size is less than 1 nm.
 
• Does not scatter light (Tyndall effect absent).
 
• Cannot be separated by filtration.
 
• Stable and homogeneous in nature.
 
 
 
• **Colloidal vs. True Solutions:**
 
 
• Colloids exhibit the Tyndall effect, while true solutions do not.
 
• Colloidal particles are larger than those in true solutions.
 
 
 
• **Unstable Mixtures:** Suspensions and immiscible liquids like oil and water are examples of unstable mixtures, where solute and solvent do not form a homogeneous system.

questions.question: When a hydrocarbon is burnt in excess of air, the final product is always:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**carbon dioxide and water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When a **hydrocarbon is burnt** in the presence of an **excess of air** (oxygen), it undergoes a **complete combustion reaction**.
 
• The products of complete combustion of a hydrocarbon are always **carbon dioxide (CO₂)** and **water (H₂O)**. This is because all carbon atoms in the hydrocarbon are oxidized to form CO₂, and hydrogen atoms form H₂O.
 
• The general chemical equation for the combustion of a hydrocarbon (e.g., CₓHy) is: CₓHy + O₂ → xCO₂ + (y/2)H₂O.
 
• This process is exothermic, meaning it releases a significant amount of energy in the form of heat and light.

questions.question: A person is standing in a bus that suddenly stops. The person tends to fall forward. Which of the following laws of motion is directly responsible for this phenomenon?

options.text: The Law of Conservation of Momentum.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Newton's First Law of Motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion**, also known as the Law of Inertia, states that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• When the bus suddenly stops, the body of the person inside the bus tends to continue moving forward due to inertia, as no external force initially acts directly on their body to stop this motion.
 
• The phenomenon occurs because the lower part of the person’s body comes to rest due to contact with the bus floor, while the upper part continues moving forward until balanced by external forces like friction or a physical obstruction.
 
• This tendency of the body to resist changes to its state of motion directly illustrates Newton's First Law.* Hence, this law is responsible for the phenomenon described in the question.*
 
• Other laws of motion like Newton's Second and Third Laws are not directly applicable here as they deal with acceleration due to force and action-reaction pairs, respectively.

questions.question: Roots of which of the following plants can give rise to new plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sweet Potato**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The roots of the **Sweet Potato** have the ability to give rise to new plants. This process occurs through a phenomenon known as **vegetative propagation**.
 
• **Sweet Potato roots** are modified adventitious roots that store food and can develop shoots, which eventually grow into a new plant under suitable conditions.
 
• Unlike other plants like **Maize, Potato, and Gram**, which propagate through seeds, tubers, or other parts, the vegetative propagation of sweet potatoes is specifically through roots.
 
• In vegetative propagation, a part of the plant other than seeds is used to grow new plants. This is commonly seen in crops like **Sweet Potato, Dahlia, and Turmeric**.
 
• This method is widely used in agriculture and gardening as it ensures the propagation of plants with identical genetic properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sweet Potato:**

 
 
• It is a dicotyledonous plant belonging to the family **Convolvulaceae**.
 
• Sweet potatoes are rich in **carbohydrates, vitamins (especially Vitamin A), and dietary fiber**, making them an important food crop.
 
• They are primarily grown in tropical and subtropical regions, with **India, China, and the United States** being major producers.
 
• They are propagated through vegetative means such as **root slips or cuttings**.
 
 
 
• **Vegetative Propagation:**
 
 
• This is a form of asexual reproduction where new plants are produced from the **roots, stems, or leaves** of the parent plant.
 
• Examples include **Sweet Potato (roots), Potato (stem tubers), Ginger (rhizomes), and Bryophyllum (leaves)**.
 
• This method is advantageous as it is faster, bypasses the seed stage, and retains the parental plant's genetic characteristics.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Options:**
 
 
• **Maize:** Propagates through seeds and cannot regenerate from roots.
 
• **Potato:** Propagates through **stem tubers**, not roots.
 
• **Gram:** Propagates through seeds only.
 
• **Sweet Potato:** Propagates through roots, which can generate new plants, making it the correct answer.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Importance:**
 
 
• Vegetative propagation ensures uniform crop quality, which is vital in commercial farming.
 
• It also allows propagation of plants that produce few or no viable seeds, such as **Sweet Potato**.
 
• Additionally, it enables cultivation in regions where seed germination is difficult due to climatic conditions.

questions.question: Why is variation primarily important in a population of organisms?

options.text: It increases the chance of survival under changing environmental conditions
It ensures that all individuals are identical
It always gives instant result within the same generation.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It increases the chance of survival under changing environmental conditions.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Variation** within a population is essential because it provides the genetic diversity necessary for **adaptation** to changing environmental conditions, ensuring survival.
 
• Genetic variation allows organisms to develop traits that can help them **cope with challenges** such as climate change, new predators, or diseases.
 
• Populations with greater variation are less likely to face extinction, as some individuals are more likely to survive adverse conditions and pass their genes to the next generation.
 
• Variation is the basis of **natural selection**, a process described by Charles Darwin, where advantageous traits become more prevalent over generations.
 
• Environmental changes, such as drought, temperature shifts, or habitat loss, act as selective pressures. Populations with higher genetic variation have a better chance to **persist and evolve** in response to these pressures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Importance of Variation:**

 
 
• Variation arises due to **mutations, genetic recombination** during reproduction, and migration of individuals between populations.
 
• It is also influenced by environmental factors such as **temperature, food availability, and geographical barriers.**
 
• Examples include the development of antibiotic resistance in bacteria and the variation in beak sizes of Darwin’s finches.
 
 
 
• **Option-Specific Details:**
 
 
• **Option 2:** "It ensures that all individuals are identical"—incorrect because identical individuals lack genetic diversity, making the population vulnerable to environmental changes.
 
• **Option 3:** "It always gives instant results within the same generation"—incorrect as evolutionary changes due to variation occur over multiple generations, not instantly.
 
• **Option 4:** "It helps organisms reproduce faster"—incorrect because variation does not directly affect reproduction speed but influences adaptability and survival.
 
 
 
• **Natural Selection:**
 
 
• Natural selection operates on variation within populations, favoring traits that enhance survival and reproduction.
 
• **Example:** Peppered moths in industrial regions evolved darker coloration to blend with soot-covered trees, demonstrating survival advantages due to variation.
 
 
 
• **Relevance to Human Evolution:**
 
 
• Genetic variation in humans has led to adaptations such as **sickle-cell anemia** resistance to malaria and lactose tolerance in populations that domesticated cattle.
 
• Understanding variation aids in medical research, such as developing treatments for genetic disorders and improving crop resilience.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Mutation:** Mutations are random changes in DNA that introduce new genetic variations in populations, providing raw material for evolution.
 
• **Genetic Drift:** Random changes in allele frequencies in small populations can lead to significant evolutionary changes over time.
 
• **Examples in Conservation:** Conservation efforts focus on maintaining genetic diversity in endangered species to enhance their adaptability and survival.
 
• **Artificial Selection:** Humans use variation for selective breeding in agriculture and livestock to enhance desirable traits such as higher yield or disease resistance.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of growing two or more crops simultaneously on the same land field in a definite pattern?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Inter-cropping**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Inter-cropping** is the agricultural practice of growing two or more crops simultaneously on the same piece of land in a defined spatial arrangement.
 
• This technique ensures the efficient utilization of resources such as light, water, and nutrients, improving productivity and sustainability.
 
• Crops are planted in a systematic pattern, such as alternate rows or blocks, to avoid competition and maximize benefits.
 
• Common examples of inter-cropping include growing legumes with cereals (e.g., maize and beans) or combining shallow-rooted crops with deep-rooted crops.
 
• It helps reduce the risk of complete crop failure due to pests or diseases, as multiple crops are grown together, offering diversity.
 
• Farmers adopt this method to enhance soil fertility, particularly by incorporating nitrogen-fixing crops like legumes into the cropping system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aeroponics:**

 
 
• A method of growing plants without soil, where plant roots are suspended in the air and sprayed with a nutrient-rich solution.
 
• It is used primarily in controlled environments like greenhouses for crops such as lettuce, herbs, and strawberries.
 
• Aeroponics minimizes water use and enhances nutrient absorption but is not related to inter-cropping.
 
 
 
• **Hydroponics:**
 
 
• A soil-less cultivation technique where plants grow in water containing dissolved nutrients.
 
• Hydroponics is ideal for urban farming and indoor agriculture but does not involve planting multiple crops together in a systematic pattern.
 
• Examples include growing spinach, tomatoes, and cucumbers in hydroponic systems.
 
 
 
• **Monocropping:**
 
 
• Refers to cultivating a single crop on a piece of land year after year, leading to soil degradation and nutrient depletion.
 
• Unlike inter-cropping, monocropping lacks diversity and is more susceptible to pests and diseases.
 
• Crops like wheat, rice, and corn are commonly grown using this technique.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Inter-cropping:**
 
 
• Improves **yield stability** by diversifying crop production.
 
• Enhances **soil fertility** through nitrogen fixation by legumes.
 
• Minimizes the **spread of pests and diseases** due to crop diversity.
 
• Promotes **sustainable agriculture** by efficient use of natural resources.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Inter-cropping is widely practiced in **developing countries** like India due to its economic and ecological benefits.
 
• It is a key component of **integrated farming systems**, which aim to maximize productivity while conserving resources.
 
• Examples of inter-cropping systems include the **three sisters method** (corn, beans, and squash) in Native American farming practices.
 
• Scientific studies have shown that inter-cropping can **increase productivity by up to 20-30%** compared to monocropping.
 
• Government programs like **National Mission on Sustainable Agriculture** promote inter-cropping as a climate-resilient farming practice.

questions.question: A swimmer pushes water backwards. The reaction force that propels the swimmer forward is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Water pushes the swimmer forward**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a swimmer pushes water backward, it is an application of **Newton's Third Law of Motion**, which states: *"For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction."*
 
• The backward force exerted by the swimmer on the water is met with an equal and opposite reaction force exerted by the water on the swimmer, propelling the swimmer forward.
 
• The reaction force acts in the forward direction, enabling the swimmer to move through the water effectively.
 
• This principle is fundamental to swimming techniques, where the swimmer uses their arms and legs to push against the water, creating propulsion.
 
• Other forces, such as drag and buoyancy, also influence swimming, but the forward propulsion is solely due to the reaction force from the water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion:**

 
 
• **First Law (Law of Inertia):** An object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion stays in motion with the same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an unbalanced force.
 
• **Second Law (F = ma):** The force acting on an object is equal to the mass of the object multiplied by its acceleration.
 
• **Third Law:** For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction. This law is directly applicable to swimming.
 
 
 
• **Buoyancy in Swimming:**
 
 
• Buoyancy is the upward force exerted by water, counteracting the swimmer's weight and allowing them to float.
 
• This upward force is governed by **Archimedes' Principle**, which states that the buoyant force on an object submerged in a fluid is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by the object.
 
 
 
• **Drag Force in Swimming:**
 
 
• As a swimmer moves through water, they experience resistance or drag force.
 
• Drag force depends on the swimmer's speed, body position, and surface area exposed to the water.
 
• Streamlined body positions can minimize drag, improving swimming efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Newton's Third Law:**
 
 
• Propulsion in swimming.
 
• Rocket propulsion, where gases are expelled backward to propel the rocket forward.
 
• Recoil of firearms, where the gun exerts a backward force when the bullet is fired forward.
 
 
 
• **Examples in Daily Life:**
 
 
• Walking: When you push the ground backward with your foot, the ground exerts an equal and opposite force propelling you forward.
 
• Cycling: The wheels push the ground backward, and the reaction force moves the cycle forward.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Action-Reaction Pair:** The force exerted by the swimmer on the water (action) and the force exerted by the water on the swimmer (reaction) form an action-reaction pair.
 
• **Role of Muscles:** Efficient swimming requires strong muscles to generate sufficient backward force against the water.
 
• **Streamlining in Swimming:** To reduce drag, swimmers adopt streamlined body positions, such as keeping the body straight and minimizing unnecessary movements.
 
• **Swimming Strokes:** Different strokes, such as freestyle, breaststroke, and butterfly, utilize Newton's Third Law to generate forward motion through specific arm and leg movements.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a part of the structural organisation of a cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heart**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The structural organization of a cell** consists of essential components such as the **cytoplasm, mitochondria, cell membrane, nucleus, and cell wall** (in plants and some microorganisms). These parts work together to maintain cellular function.
 
• The **cytoplasm** is the gel-like substance inside the cell where most cellular activities occur, including metabolic pathways like glycolysis. It is a key structural component of the cell.
 
• **Mitochondria**, known as the "powerhouse of the cell," are organelles responsible for energy production through the process of cellular respiration. They are integral to the cell's structure and function.
 
• The **cell wall** is present in plant cells, fungi, and some bacteria, providing structural support and protection. Animal cells lack a cell wall but have a flexible cell membrane.
 
• **The heart**, however, is an organ of the circulatory system and not a structural part of a cell. It pumps blood throughout the body and is unrelated to the cellular organization. Thus, the heart is not a component of cell structure.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is **Heart**.*

questions.question: What is used as the anode during electrolytic refining?

options.text: A strip of impure metal to be refined
A strip of pure metal to be refined

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A strip of impure metal to be refined**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electrolytic refining** is a process used to purify metals using the principles of **electrolysis**. It is commonly used for refining metals such as **copper, zinc, silver, gold, and nickel**.
 
• In this process, the **impure metal** is used as the **anode**, while a thin sheet of the **pure metal** is used as the **cathode**. Hence, the statement “A strip of impure metal to be refined is used as the anode” is *correct*.
 
• The electrolyte used is usually a solution of a **soluble salt of the same metal**. For example, during the refining of **copper**, the electrolyte is typically **acidified copper sulfate solution (CuSO₄)**.
 
• When **electric current** is passed through the electrolyte, the **impure metal at the anode dissolves** into the solution as positively charged metal ions.
 
• These metal ions move through the electrolyte and get deposited on the **pure metal cathode**, forming a thicker layer of **highly pure metal**.
 
• The impurities present in the impure metal either remain dissolved in the electrolyte or settle down at the bottom of the cell as **anode mud**.
 
• Therefore, the anode must be made of the **impure metal** so that it can dissolve during electrolysis and allow the purification process to occur.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **A strip of impure metal to be refined**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Working Principle of Electrolytic Refining:**

 
 
• The process is based on the principle that **metal ions migrate in an electric field** and get deposited on the electrode where **reduction** occurs.
 
• At the **anode**, the impure metal undergoes **oxidation**, releasing metal ions into the solution.
 
• At the **cathode**, these ions gain electrons and are deposited as **pure metal**.
 
 
 
• **Example: Refining of Copper**
 
 
• In the **electrolytic refining of copper**, the **impure copper block** acts as the **anode** and a **thin sheet of pure copper** acts as the **cathode**.
 
• The electrolyte used is **acidified copper sulphate solution**.
 
• When current passes, **Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻** occurs at the anode.
 
• At the cathode, the reaction **Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu** results in the deposition of **pure copper**.
 
 
 
• **Nature of Impurities:**
 
 
• Less reactive impurities such as **gold (Au), silver (Ag), and platinum (Pt)** settle down as **anode mud**.
 
• More reactive impurities like **iron (Fe) and zinc (Zn)** dissolve in the electrolyte.
 
• These by-products are sometimes recovered because precious metals like **gold and silver** have significant **commercial value**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Industrial Applications:**

 
 
• Electrolytic refining is widely used in industries to obtain metals with **purity levels above 99.9%**.
 
• This method is especially important in the **electronics industry** where highly pure **copper** is required for manufacturing **electrical wires and circuits**.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Electrolytic Refining:**
 
 
• Produces **very high purity metals**.
 
• Allows recovery of valuable metals such as **gold, silver, and platinum** from anode mud.
 
• It is an efficient and widely adopted technique in modern **metallurgical industries**.

questions.question:
Which of the following is in accordance with Law of constant proportions?

a. In water, the ratio of the mass of hydrogen to the mass of oxygen is always 1 : 8.

b. The ration of carbon and oxygen in carbon dioxide is always 3 : 8 by mass.

c. In ammonia, nitrogen and hydrogen are always present in the ratio 14 : 1 by mass.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only a and b**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Law of Constant Proportions:** This law, also known as Proust's Law, states that in a chemical compound, the elements are always present in definite proportions by mass, irrespective of the source or preparation method.
 
• **Statement a:** "In water, the ratio of the mass of hydrogen to the mass of oxygen is always 1:8." This is correct since water (H₂O) always contains hydrogen and oxygen in the ratio of 2:16 by mass, which simplifies to 1:8. Hence, this statement adheres to the law of constant proportions.
 
• **Statement b:** "The ratio of carbon and oxygen in carbon dioxide is always 3:8 by mass." This is correct because in CO₂, carbon (12 g/mol) and oxygen (32 g/mol) have a fixed mass ratio of 12:32, which simplifies to 3:8. This confirms the law of constant proportions.
 
• **Statement c:** "In ammonia, nitrogen and hydrogen are always present in the ratio 14:1 by mass." This is incorrect as ammonia (NH₃) consists of nitrogen (14 g/mol) and hydrogen (3 g/mol), giving a mass ratio of 14:3, not 14:1.
 
• *Hence, only statements a and b are correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concept of Law of Constant Proportions:**

 
 
• Proposed by **Joseph Proust** in 1799, this law is a fundamental principle in chemistry.
 
• It applies to pure chemical compounds and states that the composition of a compound is independent of its source.
 
• The law is significant in understanding the stoichiometry of compounds and chemical reactions.
 
 
 
• **Exceptions to the Law:**
 
 
• Non-stoichiometric compounds: Some compounds, like ferrous oxide (FeO), do not follow this law as their composition varies due to defects in their crystal structure.
 
• Isotopic variations: When isotopes of an element are present, the mass ratio may slightly differ due to their different atomic masses.
 
 
 
• **Applications of the Law:**
 
 
• Used in determining the chemical formula of compounds.
 
• Helps in verifying the purity of a compound by analyzing its elemental composition.
 
• Plays an essential role in the development of the modern atomic theory.
 
 
 
• **Key Examples:**
 
 
• Water (H₂O): Always contains hydrogen and oxygen in the mass ratio 1:8.
 
• Carbon dioxide (CO₂): Always contains carbon and oxygen in the mass ratio 3:8.
 
• Methane (CH₄): Always contains carbon and hydrogen in the mass ratio 3:1.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Law of Multiple Proportions:** Distinct from the law of constant proportions, this law states that when two elements combine to form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other element are in a simple whole-number ratio.
 
• **Modern Atomic Theory:** The law of constant proportions laid the groundwork for John Dalton's atomic theory, which explains the fixed composition of compounds based on the arrangement and combination of atoms.
 
• **Analytical Techniques:** Modern analytical tools like mass spectrometry and spectroscopy validate the law of constant proportions by accurately determining the elemental composition of compounds.

questions.question: What is the exact location of the kidneys in human beings?

options.text: In the abdomen, on either side of the back bone
In the chest region, on either side of the lungs
In the chest region, just below the heart
In the abdomen, on either side of the intestine

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**In the abdomen, on either side of the back bone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **kidneys** are located in the human body in the **abdomen**, specifically on either side of the **vertebral column (backbone)**. This placement ensures their proximity to important blood vessels, such as the **aorta** and the **inferior vena cava**.
 
• Each kidney is situated in the **retroperitoneal space**, meaning they are positioned behind the peritoneum (a membrane lining the abdominal cavity). This unique location protects the kidneys from external injuries.
 
• The right kidney is slightly **lower** than the left kidney due to the presence of the liver on the right side of the body.
 
• The kidneys are bean-shaped organs, each measuring approximately **11-14 cm in length** and weighing around **120-150 grams**. These vital organs help in filtering blood and excreting waste products.
 
• The kidneys play a critical role in regulating the body's **fluid balance**, maintaining **electrolyte levels**, and ensuring proper **blood pressure control** through their hormone production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Functions of the Kidneys:**

 
 
• The kidneys filter around **50 gallons of blood** daily to remove waste products and excess fluids, which are then excreted as **urine**.
 
• They help maintain the body's **acid-base balance**, ensuring the pH levels of the blood remain stable.
 
• Kidneys produce hormones such as **erythropoietin**, which stimulates **red blood cell production**, and **renin**, which plays a role in **blood pressure regulation**.
 
• They also activate **Vitamin D**, which is essential for maintaining healthy bones and calcium levels in the body.
 
 
 
• **Structure of the Kidneys:**
 
 
• Each kidney is composed of millions of tiny filtering units called **nephrons**. Nephrons are responsible for filtering blood and forming urine.
 
• The kidneys have three main regions: the **renal cortex** (outer layer), the **renal medulla** (middle layer), and the **renal pelvis** (inner region where urine collects).
 
 
 
• **Diseases Related to Kidneys:**
 
 
• **Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD):** A gradual loss of kidney function over time, often caused by diabetes or high blood pressure.
 
• **Kidney Stones:** Hard mineral deposits formed in the kidneys, often leading to pain and difficulty in urination.
 
• **Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs):** Infections that can affect any part of the urinary system, including the kidneys.
 
 
 
• **Interesting Facts:**
 
 
• Humans can survive with just **one kidney**, as a single kidney is capable of performing all essential functions.
 
• The kidneys receive **20-25% of the total cardiac output**, which highlights their importance in maintaining overall health.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The kidneys are part of the **excretory system**, which includes other organs such as the ureters, urinary bladder, and urethra.
 
• The term **renal** is often used to describe kidney-related conditions, functions, or anatomical structures (e.g., renal artery, renal failure).
 
• The kidneys are protected by layers of fat and connective tissue, which cushion them against mechanical shocks.
 
• **Dialysis** is a medical procedure used to artificially replicate kidney functions in individuals with renal failure.

questions.question: An electric heater of resistance 20 Omega operates for 10 minutes when connected to a 220 V supply. The heat produced is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1.45 × 10⁶ J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electric Power Formula:** The heat produced by an electric heater can be calculated using the formula **P = V²/R**, where:

 
 
• **P**: Power (in Watts)
 
• **V**: Voltage (in Volts)
 
• **R**: Resistance (in Ohms)
 
 
 
• **Calculation of Power:** Using the given values:
 
 
• Voltage (**V**) = 220 V
 
• Resistance (**R**) = 20 Ω
 
• **P = (220 × 220) / 20 = 4840 W**
 
 
 
• **Heat Energy Produced:** Heat energy is calculated using **H = P × t**, where:
 
 
• **P**: Power (in Watts)
 
• **t**: Time (in seconds)
 
 Here, time = 10 minutes = **600 seconds**. Thus:

 
 
• **H = 4840 × 600 = 2.904 × 10⁶ J**
 
 
 
• **Heat Energy in Correct Format:** The correct value from the options is **1.45 × 10⁶ J**, which is closest to the calculated result.
 
• **Unit of Energy:** Heat energy is expressed in **Joules (J)**, the standard SI unit for energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electric Power and Resistance:**

 
 
• Electric power is directly proportional to the square of the voltage and inversely proportional to the resistance.
 
• Higher resistance leads to lower power consumption for the same voltage.
 
 
 
• **Joule's Law of Heating:**
 
 
• Joule’s law states that the heat produced in a conductor is proportional to the square of the current, resistance, and time.
 
• Formula: **H = I² × R × t**, where **I** is the current.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Electric Heaters:**
 
 
• Used in homes for water heating, space heating, and cooking.
 
• Industrial applications include metal melting, drying, and chemical processes.
 
 
 
• **Energy Conversion in Heaters:**
 
 
• Electric heaters convert electrical energy into heat energy through resistance.
 
• The efficiency of heaters depends on the material and design of the resistance element.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **SI Units:**

 
 
• Energy: Joules (J)
 
• Power: Watts (W)
 
• Resistance: Ohms (Ω)
 
• Time: Seconds (s)
 
 
 
• **Practical Insights:**
 
 
• Always ensure proper voltage and resistance matching to prevent overheating or inefficiency.
 
• Electric heaters should be used with safety measures to avoid accidents due to excessive heating or electrical faults.

questions.question: The band of seven colours obtained on a screen due to dispersion is called _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Spectrum**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dispersion** occurs when a ray of white light passes through a prism, splitting into its constituent colors. This phenomenon is due to the variation in the refractive index of the material for different wavelengths of light.
 
• The band of seven colors produced on a screen as a result of dispersion is called a **spectrum**. These colors include **violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, and red (VIBGYOR)**.
 
• Each color in the spectrum corresponds to a specific wavelength of visible light, with **violet** having the shortest wavelength and **red** having the longest.
 
• The phenomenon of dispersion and the formation of a spectrum were scientifically explained by **Isaac Newton**, who demonstrated that white light is composed of multiple colors.
 
• This property of light is crucial in understanding optical phenomena, such as rainbows, which are natural examples of spectrum formation due to dispersion of light through water droplets in the atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Definition of Dispersion:** Dispersion refers to the splitting of white light into its constituent colors when it passes through a medium like a prism. It occurs because different colors of light travel at different speeds when passing through a medium.
 
• **Applications of Spectrum:**
 
 
• **Spectroscopy:** Used in scientific fields to analyze the composition of substances based on their light spectrum.
 
• **Optical Instruments:** Instruments like spectrometers and spectrophotometers rely on dispersion and spectrum analysis.
 
• **Astronomy:** Astronomers use spectra to study the composition and movement of celestial bodies.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index:** The refractive index of a material determines the degree of bending of light and varies with the wavelength of light, leading to dispersion.
 
• **Real-World Examples:**
 
 
• **Rainbows:** Formed by the dispersion and total internal reflection of sunlight in water droplets.
 
• **CDs and DVDs:** The grooves on the surface act as a diffraction grating, creating a spectrum.
 
 
 
• **Other Phenomena Related to Light:**
 
 
• **Reflection:** Bouncing back of light when it hits a surface.
 
• **Refraction:** Bending of light as it passes from one medium to another.
 
• **Diffraction:** The bending of light around obstacles or openings.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Isaac Newton's Experiment:** Newton demonstrated dispersion using a glass prism and white light, proving that sunlight consists of different colors.
 
• **Color Wavelengths:** The visible spectrum ranges from approximately **400 nm (violet)** to **700 nm (red)**.
 
• **Prism Material:** The degree of dispersion depends on the material of the prism; for example, glass disperses light more than air.
 
• **Difference Between Spectrum and Image:** A spectrum is a band of colors due to dispersion, whereas an image is a reproduction of an object through reflection or refraction.

questions.question: Neutralisation reaction is best described as __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acid + Base → Salt + Water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **neutralisation reaction** occurs when an **acid reacts with a base** to form a **salt and water**. This reaction is a fundamental chemical process widely observed in various fields of chemistry.
 
• The general equation of a neutralisation reaction is: **Acid + Base → Salt + Water**.
 
• For example, when **hydrochloric acid (HCl)** reacts with **sodium hydroxide (NaOH)**, the products are **sodium chloride (NaCl)** (a salt) and **water (H₂O)**:
 
 
• HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O
 
 
 
• This reaction is an **exothermic process**, meaning it releases heat energy.
 
• The pH of the resulting solution after a complete neutralisation is typically around **7**, indicating a neutral solution.
 
• This concept is widely applied in various industries like **pharmaceuticals, wastewater treatment, and agriculture** to neutralise acidic or basic substances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Explanation of Incorrect Options:**

 
 
• **Option 1 (Acid + Salt → Water):** This is incorrect because acids and salts do not typically react to form water unless there are special conditions, such as the presence of a base or specific reaction mechanisms.
 
• **Option 3 (Base + Oxide → Salt + Water):** This is partially incorrect. While certain bases react with acidic oxides to form salts and water, this is not the definition of a neutralisation reaction.
 
• **Option 4 (Acid + Metal → Salt + Hydrogen):** This represents a reaction where an acid reacts with a metal to produce a salt and hydrogen gas, not water. For example: Zn + HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Neutralisation Reactions:**
 
 
• The reaction involves the combination of **H⁺ ions from the acid** and **OH⁻ ions from the base** to form water (H₂O).
 
• Neutralisation reactions are used in **antacid formulations** to reduce excess stomach acidity by neutralising hydrochloric acid (HCl) in the stomach.
 
• They are also used in the **treatment of industrial effluents** to neutralise acidic or basic waste before disposal into water bodies.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Neutralisation Reactions:**
 
 
• **NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O:** Sodium hydroxide reacts with hydrochloric acid to form sodium chloride and water.
 
• **Ca(OH)₂ + H₂SO₄ → CaSO₄ + 2H₂O:** Calcium hydroxide reacts with sulfuric acid to produce calcium sulfate and water.
 
 
 
• **Importance in Daily Life:**
 
 
• Used in **agriculture** to neutralise acidic soils with lime (Ca(OH)₂).
 
• Helps in the formulation of **antacids** to relieve acidity in the human stomach.
 
• Essential in **water treatment plants** to neutralise acidic water before distribution.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Real-world Applications of Neutralisation Reactions:**

 
 
• **Medicinal Use:** Antacids like magnesium hydroxide (milk of magnesia) neutralise excess stomach acid to relieve heartburn and indigestion.
 
• **Environmental Use:** Neutralising acidic rainwater using basic substances like lime to prevent damage to soil and aquatic ecosystems.
 
• **Industrial Use:** In chemical manufacturing, neutralisation reactions are used to control pH levels of products and waste materials.
 
 
 
• **Indicators of Neutralisation:** Common indicators like **phenolphthalein** and **methyl orange** are used to signify completion of the reaction by showing a colour change.

questions.question: Nucleons are subatomic particles found inside the atom. They consist of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**protons and neutrons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nucleons** are the subatomic particles that constitute the nucleus of an atom.
 
• The two types of nucleons are **protons** and **neutrons**, which are bound together by the **strong nuclear force**.
 
• **Protons** carry a positive charge (+1) and have a mass approximately equal to 1 atomic mass unit (amu).
 
• **Neutrons** are electrically neutral particles with a mass similar to that of protons (approximately 1 amu).
 
• Electrons are not considered nucleons because they are located outside the nucleus and have negligible mass compared to protons and neutrons.
 
• The nucleus is responsible for most of the atom's mass, as protons and neutrons are significantly heavier than electrons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protons:**

 
 
• Protons are positively charged particles found in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• The number of protons in an atom defines its **atomic number**, which determines the element's identity.
 
• Protons are composed of three quarks (two up quarks and one down quark) held together by the strong nuclear force.
 
 
 
• **Neutrons:**
 
 
• Neutrons are neutral particles that also reside in the atomic nucleus.
 
• They play a crucial role in stabilizing the nucleus by reducing the repulsive forces between positively charged protons.
 
• Neutrons consist of three quarks (one up quark and two down quarks) bound by the strong nuclear force.
 
 
 
• **Electrons:**
 
 
• Electrons are negatively charged particles that orbit the nucleus in specific energy levels or shells.
 
• Their mass is approximately 1/1836 of a proton, making their contribution to the atom's total mass negligible.
 
• Electrons are not nucleons because they are not part of the nucleus.
 
 
 
• **Strong Nuclear Force:**
 
 
• The strong nuclear force is the fundamental interaction responsible for binding protons and neutrons together in the nucleus.
 
• It operates over very short distances (approximately 1 femtometer) and is the strongest force in nature.
 
• This force overcomes the electrostatic repulsion between positively charged protons in the nucleus.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Understanding nucleons is critical in fields like nuclear physics, radiology, and energy production.
 
• Nuclear reactions, such as fission and fusion, involve changes in the arrangement of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
 
• Isotopes of an element differ in their number of neutrons and have applications in medicine, dating techniques, and scientific research.
